decision: Both register-distributed variants rejected; exact previous 256-thread shared-memory solver restored. Installed module was never changed.

method.workload: Recorded 22-stone scene, all dynamic, repeated independently across batches. 100 timesteps; 3D/4D; batches 32/128.
method.repetitions: One cold call plus three warm calls per case; warm median shown.
method.timing: Fresh sequential processes with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1. Native run includes host preparation, transfers, physics and output construction. Fingerprints are outside timing.
method.baseline: Previously retained 256-thread shared-factor implementation; installed binary preserved and used via an isolated baseline package.
method.scope: This experiment changes only velocity triangular substitution, not factorization, physical tolerances or solver limits.
limitations: No new full MCTS benchmark: neither variant passed the 4D rollout speed gate.
Compiler resource counts are static. Achieved occupancy and instruction-stall counters were not collected.
Increased register pressure and extra shuffle/control work are plausible costs, not separately measured causes.
The unrolled variant passed tolerance-based native regressions but failed the stricter exact 4D rollout comparison.
